study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression normative models to estimate FCS as a function of age and sex in healthy controls.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: First, we evaluated the performance of the Gaussian process regression model in predicting FCS values within HCs through 10-fold crossvalidation. Subsequently, for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values as a function of age and sex within HCs.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Functional connectivity strength (FCS) values for each brain region derived from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: the Functional Connectivity Strength (FCS) values for each brain region were calculated as the aggregate of connectivity between the given region and all other regions.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as predictors in the normative models.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values as a function of age and sex within HCs.
